market_summary: Markets are being whipsawed by an unprecedented corporate-governance crisis at Nvidia: reports of a board deliberation over ousting CEO Jensen Huang over alleged affairs have wiped ~$600bn off NVDA and dragged broader AI-linked tech (QQQ, META, GOOGL) lower in sympathy on Nov 12. Meanwhile Alphabet's Google Cloud delivered standout Q3 growth (103% YoY, margins to 36.2%), a fundamental positive that's been overshadowed by the tech-wide risk-off tone. In Singapore, Q3 bank earnings diverged — OCBC beat while DBS and UOB missed on NIM compression — and SGX posted strong October volumes (turnover +32% YoY) even as its own shares have lagged. Overall: elevated single-stock idiosyncratic risk in US mega-cap tech, and a split SGX picture between resilient volume/fee-driven names and margin-squeezed banks.

picks.thesis: An active board deliberation over removing CEO Jensen Huang is a rare, high-impact governance shock for the world's most important AI chip supplier. Even if Huang survives, the overhang of leadership uncertainty into the Nov 17 earnings date, combined with already-elevated volatility (38.6% annualized) and 2x normal volume, points to further downside or at least continued whipsaw before any resolution. Shares are already down 24% over 1 month and 27% off highs, but the catalyst is still unresolved as of today.
picks.news: Nvidia board met Nov 11 to decide on Jensen Huang's status after affair allegations; stock down ~7-8% in European/extended trading Nov 12, erasing ~$600bn in value since the probe was announced (CNBC, Nov 12).
picks.risks: If the board publicly reaffirms Huang or resolves the matter quickly with no departure, shares could snap back sharply given still-bullish analyst base (57 buy ratings) and cheap-looking valuation after the drop; earnings on Nov 17 could also override the governance story if results are strong.

picks.thesis: Google Cloud's Q3 results (103% revenue growth, margin expansion to 36.2%) show Alphabet's AI infrastructure business scaling profitably, yet the stock is down 17% over the past month and 27% off its 52-week high — a disconnect partly driven by the broad AI-sector selloff triggered by the Nvidia crisis rather than anything specific to Alphabet's fundamentals. Analyst consensus implies 36% upside, the highest of the mega-caps covered here.
picks.news: Google Cloud revenue +103% YoY to $30.7bn with operating margin expansion to 36.2% (SEC 10-Q filing, reported Oct 28 — note this is a background catalyst, not fresh news, but the subsequent price decline looks overdone relative to it).
picks.risks: If the Nvidia-driven AI capex pullback narrative broadens into real demand destruction for cloud/AI infrastructure, Alphabet's cloud growth could decelerate; continued antitrust or regulatory overhangs are also a risk not reflected in the price stats.

picks.thesis: OCBC was the only major Singapore bank to beat Q3 2026 estimates (profit +3% YoY) while DBS and UOB both missed on NIM compression, yet OCBC's stock has still fallen in sympathy with the sector (-1.8% 1m, -9.8% 3m). This relative fundamental outperformance versus peers that haven't been reflected in price looks like a mean-reversion opportunity within the sector.
picks.news: OCBC Q3 2026 net profit +3% YoY to S$2.04bn, beating expectations, vs. DBS -5% and UOB missing forecasts (thekopinotes.com, Nov 4-6).
picks.risks: Sector-wide NIM compression from rate-cut expectations could still weigh on all SG banks regardless of individual earnings quality; OCBC's 52w-high drawdown of -11% suggests broader de-rating risk that could continue.

picks.thesis: SGX reported October securities turnover up 32% YoY and derivatives volumes at a six-month high, both leading indicators of strong fee income for the exchange's next earnings print. The stock has nonetheless fallen 17.8% over 3 months and sits 19% below its 52-week high, creating a gap between improving operating metrics and a depressed share price.
picks.news: SGX October securities turnover +32% YoY to S$44.8bn; derivatives daily volume at highest level since April (Tipranks, Nov 11).
picks.risks: Volume strength can be episodic (e.g., driven by the current market volatility itself) rather than a durable trend; a market calm-down could reverse the turnover tailwind, and the stock's hold-heavy analyst rating (9 hold vs 6 buy) suggests limited near-term re-rating conviction.

picks.thesis: UOB was the weakest of the three Singapore banks this earnings season, missing Q3 profit expectations on margin compression, and carries the most negative sell-side skew of the trio (5 buy/9 hold/2 sell) with price already down 16% from its 52-week high and trading below both its 50- and 200-day averages, suggesting continued underperformance versus OCBC.
picks.news: UOB Q3 2026 profit of S$1.25bn missed expectations amid margin compression (thekopinotes.com, Nov 4).
picks.risks: Much of the bad news may already be priced in given the stock's larger drawdown versus peers; a broader SGX bank-sector bounce (e.g., on rate stabilization) would lift all three names together and squeeze this short.

picks.thesis: The Nvidia governance crisis is a Nasdaq-100 wide risk given NVDA's large index weight and the knock-on sentiment hit to other AI-levered names (META, GOOGL, MSFT all down over the past month). QQQ is already down 7.2% over 1 month and trading below its 50-day average, and further NVDA headline volatility into its Nov 17 earnings could keep pressuring the index.
picks.news: Broad tech selloff Nov 12 tied to Nvidia CEO uncertainty, with major Nasdaq names declining in sympathy (CNBC, Nov 12).
picks.risks: Today's price action already shows QQQ up 2.3% intraday, suggesting dip-buying; a resolution of the Nvidia situation or strong earnings from mega-caps could quickly reverse the pressure given still-strong fundamentals at Amazon, Apple, and Microsoft.
